title: The base image and the start commands
body:
## Summary

Every release now builds the worker's base image, and a project's page shows the two commands that build that project's worker from its own `.devflow/Dockerfile` and start it. The owner pastes them into a terminal on the Mac mini. When the project's recipe or the base image changes, the page says the worker needs a rebuild, and that worker gets no work until it is rebuilt.

Read it in this order:

1. **The base image**, `devflow/worker.Dockerfile`, a new concept: a build stage publishes `DevFlow.Worker` as one self contained file for the build's architecture, and the final stage is `node:26-trixie-slim` with git, ca-certificates, jq, procps, util-linux and Claude Code 2.1.325, pinned in `devflow/worker/package.json` and its lockfile. It has two users. The worker runs as root, the entrypoint, and owns `/run/devflow/` (mode 700). `agent` (uid 1000, the image's `node` user renamed) owns `/work` and has `/home/agent/.claude/settings.json` with attribution turned off. `ONBUILD` turns the build arguments `DEVFLOW_BASE` and `DEVFLOW_RECIPE_VERSION` into the variables the worker reports in `hello`. `infra/hosted/compose.yaml` builds it as `devflow-worker` with `deploy.replicas: 0`. `infra/hosted/check.sh` checks that it is built and never started, leaves it out of the root check, and runs `devflow/tests/image/base-image.test.sh` against it, under a test tag of its own.
2. **The recipe route**, `GET /devflow/api/worker/recipe` (`devflow/src/DevFlow/Recipes/`), worker scheme. It serves `.devflow/Dockerfile` from the default branch as `text/plain`, with `X-Devflow-Recipe-Version: <commit>`, `nosniff` and `no-store`, and records that version on the project (migration `0009_recipe_version`). `Recipe.FirstRefused` reads the file the way Docker's parser does: the `escape` directive, read only within the parser directives at the top up to the first line that is not a known one (`syntax`, `escape`, `check`), as BuildKit stops, joined continuations, and comment lines inside a continuation. It refuses `COPY` or `ADD` in any case, alone or after `ONBUILD`, with `422` naming the line. A missing file is `404`, and text that is not UTF-8 or is over 64 KB is `422`. The code host gains `DefaultBranchFile`. On GitHub that is the newest commit of the default branch that changed the path, then the file raw at that commit, tested against the recorded answer `contracts/github/commits-path.json`.
3. **`project.json`'s schema**: `ProjectFile` in `DevFlow.Protocol`, read strictly by hand, and `contracts/devflow/project.schema.json`, with a test that keeps the two in step.
4. **Settings and the page**: `DEVFLOW_WORKER_IMAGE` and `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL`, `WorkerStart`, which builds the two commands, the rebuild flag in `WorkerStore` (compared in SQL) with `204` from `jobs/next`, and the Workers panel in `devflow/web/src/project.tsx`.
5. **Docs**, listed under Doc changes.

Closes #334

## Tasks

- [x] Add the base image's Dockerfile and its service in `infra/hosted/compose.yaml`, with the image test and `check.sh` covering it: b354a276
- [x] Add the recipe route with its refusals, and the JSON Schema of `project.json`, with their tests: 519ba9da
- [x] Add the settings `DEVFLOW_WORKER_IMAGE` and `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL`, the commands on the project's page, and the rebuild notice, with the Vitest and e2e tests and the screenshots: 76d07074, ac780f79
- [x] Write the docs named in Settled: fe3007b9

## Decisions the agent made

- **The attribution setting**, which Settled asked to be read from Claude Code's documentation: the image writes `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": "", "sessionUrl": false}}`. The docs' settings reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md, "Git and attribution", read this run) says of `attribution.commit`: "Set it to an empty string to hide commit attribution". It says the same of `attribution.pr`. It also says "To hide all attribution, set `attribution` to `false`. In a settings file that earlier versions also read, set `commit` and `pr` to empty strings and `sessionUrl` to `false` instead." `includeCoAuthoredBy` is "Deprecated since v2.0.62". Alternative: `"attribution": false`, which needs 2.1.281 or later and makes older versions skip the whole file. Why: the object form works on 2.1.325 and on any version a later pin might go back to.
- **owner-decision. Claude Code is installed with `npm ci` from a committed lockfile** (`devflow/worker/package.json` and `package-lock.json`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` 2.1.325 with its integrity hash) into `/opt/devflow-tools`, symlinked to `/usr/local/bin/claude` so every user has it on PATH. Settled says "installed globally from npm at that exact version". Alternative: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.325`. Why: "The images" in `infra/hosted/README.md`, which the slice's Context names, has every image install only from lockfiles, and `agree.test.sh` holds images to that rule. The version is the exact one Settled pins and the command is on every user's PATH, so the intent holds. The install also checks the package's integrity.
- **The terminal fetches the recipe from the platform's public origin, not from `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL`.** Settled's command fetches from `<DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL>`, which in compose defaults to `http://host.docker.internal:9080`. That name resolves only inside Docker Desktop's containers and not on the Mac itself, where the command runs. The container's `DEVFLOW_URL` is still `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL`, as the acceptance test requires. Alternative: Settled's shape as written, which fails at its first step on the Mac. Why: Settled calls the command's shape "the intent" and leaves its details to the builder. The commands still use both settings and never hold the key.
- **The start command hands the key to `curl` on stdin** (review round 1): `sed -n 's/^DEVFLOW_PROJECT_KEY=/Authorization: Bearer /p' ~/.devflow/<project>.env | curl -fsS -H @- …`. Settled's shape has `-H "Authorization: Bearer $(sed …)"`. The alternative was Settled's shape with the security section saying the key is visible in `ps` while the fetch runs. Why: the shell expands `$(…)` before `curl` starts, so the key would be in `curl`'s arguments, which every user on the Mac mini sees in `ps` (the `agent` user among them), and `curl` hides `-u` from `ps` but not `-H`. On security, the stricter option, and the owner still pastes one block. Checked here that `curl` 8.7.1 on the Mac mini sends the header it reads from `-H @-` (`curl -v` against `https://platform.test/` showed `> Authorization: Bearer dfw_TESTKEY`).
- **The recipe check drops a byte order mark at the start of the file**, as BuildKit does on the first line, found while fixing the directive scan: without it, a recipe starting with the mark and then `ADD` was read with the instruction `\uFEFFADD`, not refused, while Docker runs it as `ADD`. A case in `CopyAndAddAreRefused` covers it.
- **How the recipe version reaches the build**, which Settled left to the builder: `curl -D` writes the response headers to `/tmp/devflow-<project>.headers`, and `awk` reads `X-Devflow-Recipe-Version` from that file, case insensitively and without the carriage return, into `--build-arg DEVFLOW_RECIPE_VERSION`. The base image's `ONBUILD` turns it into the variable the worker reports. The command's steps are joined with `&&`, so a failed fetch or build leaves the running worker in place. The key is saved in a subshell with `umask 077`, so the terminal's own umask is kept.
- **`DEVFLOW_WORKER_IMAGE` and `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL` are refused at startup unless they are safe unquoted in a shell**, because they are pasted into a command the owner runs. Alternative: quoting them in the command. Why: on security, the stricter option. A value that needs quoting is a misconfiguration, and refusing it at startup is easier to see than a command that quietly does something else. Dev stack defaults: `platform-hosted/devflow-worker:dev` and `http://host.docker.internal:8084`, Dev flow's own port as a container reaches it.
- **A project's name in the commands** comes from its repository name: lowercase, ASCII letters and digits, one hyphen between runs, at most 40 characters, and `project` if nothing is left. This keeps it a valid image name, container name and file name, and a word the shell reads as it is.
- **The fake code host's recipe version** is the SHA-256 of the file's content, so a test that changes the file changes the version, the way a commit would.
- **The migration was renumbered** from `0008` to `0009_recipe_version` when `origin/main` was merged in, because #351 (the Claude login) took `0008_claude_logins` after this branch was cut. The commit message of 519ba9da still says `0008`.
- **The recipe code is in its own namespace, `DevFlow.Recipes`**, not in `DevFlow.Workers`, whose constant-time test keeps that namespace free of string comparisons, and the recipe parser compares strings.
- **The root check in `check.sh` skips services with zero replicas**, since the base image's worker runs as root by design and is never started in the hosted project. The new case `the_worker_base_image_is_built_and_never_started` checks the image exists and no container of it does. `check.sh` therefore needs `jq`, and its header says so.

## Verification

Gate, for the areas `changed-areas.sh` printed as true (`core=true canary=true brain=true libs=false scripts=false web=true e2e=true hosted=true`, `dotnet_services` review and devflow), at c6d509c6, run locally this run on the Mac mini after `reset-db.sh` and every service's migrations:

- core (true because `contracts/` changed): `cargo fmt --check` ok; `services.sh run core migrate` ok; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` ok; `cargo test --locked` ok; `cargo test --locked --test app_roles -- --ignored` ok; `cargo sqlx prepare --check -- --all-targets --locked` (sqlx-cli 0.9.0, as `core.yml` installs) ok.
- canary: `ruff check` ok, `ruff format --check` ok, `pytest` 21 passed.
- brain: `ruff check` ok, `ruff format --check` ok, `mypy` ok, migrate ok, `pytest` 401 passed.
- web, in each folder `frontends.sh` prints: `npm ci`, `biome ci .`, `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest run`, `npm run build` all ok. Vitest: design/ui 210, Brain/web 116, devflow/web 125, review/web 128 passed.
- dotnet, review: `dotnet tool restore`, `dotnet restore --locked-mode`, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes --no-restore`, `dotnet build --no-restore -c Release`, migrate, `dotnet test` 201 passed.
- dotnet, devflow: the same steps but `dotnet tool restore`, since it has no tool manifest; `dotnet test` DevFlow.Tests 357 passed and DevFlow.Worker.Tests 50 passed. Among them are `RecipeTests.TheDockerfileIsHandedToTheProjectsKey`, `RecipeTests.CopyAndAddAreRefused`, `RecipeTests.AMissingDockerfileIsSaid`, `ProjectFileTests.ProjectJsonIsReadStrictly`, `StartCommandTests.TheCommandsNameTheImageTheAddressAndTheKeyFile`, the new `StartCommandTests.TheKeyIsNeverInAProcesssArguments` and `WorkerVersionTests.AWorkerOnAnOldRecipeGetsNoWork`.
- e2e, against the platform started from the branch (frontends built, Caddy recreated, every service healthy through `https://platform.test`): `playwright install chromium`, `pytest` 501 passed (4 deselected), including `test_the_project_page_shows_how_to_start_a_worker` and `test_the_page_says_when_a_worker_needs_a_rebuild`; `ruff check` ok; `ruff format --check` ok.
- hosted: `bash infra/hosted/check.sh` exit 0, 13 cases ok, among them `the_worker_base_image_is_built_and_never_started`, `no_container_runs_as_root`, `the_acceptance_suite_passes_against_the_containers` (504 passed) and `base_image_test`. In `devflow/tests/image/base-image.test.sh`, 5 passed: `TheImageBuilds`, `TheAgentCannotReadTheWorkersFiles` (agent cannot list or read `/run/devflow/`, `claude --version` answers 2.1.325, git and node run), `TheWorkerRunsAsRootAndTheAgentOwnsTheWork`, `CommitAttributionIsOff` and `AProjectsImageReportsItsBaseAndRecipe`.

Review round 1, failing before the fixes (at b0f1f16c with only the new test cases, `dotnet test --filter "RecipeTests.CopyAndAddAreRefused|StartCommandTests"`): 3 failed, 3 passed. `CopyAndAddAreRefused`: `Assert.Equal() Failure: Expected: 422, Actual: 200`, for the recipe with `# foo=bar` before `` # escape=` ``. `TheKeyIsNeverInAProcesssArguments`: `Assert.Contains() Failure: Sub-string not found, Not found: "-H\n@-\n"`, the recorded arguments of `curl`. `TheCommandsNameTheImageTheAddressAndTheKeyFile`: the new `sed … | curl -fsS -H @-` text not found. After the fixes, the 4 `RecipeTests` and 5 `StartCommandTests` pass.

I looked at the start-worker screenshots again at c6d509c6, since the command's text changed: it wraps inside its block at 390px and nothing overflows. The rebuild screenshots are unchanged by this round; at b0f1f16c neither layout overflowed and the notice read "Fodr's recipe has changed: run the command again". The bottom tab bar that appears partway down the phone captures is the fixed nav caught in a full page screenshot.

Acceptance tests of the first round, failing before the change: **Not verified (interrupted run).** The tests were written and committed by an earlier run of this slice that was interrupted before it opened the pull request, and their red output was lost with it. This run resumed at the merge of `main` and re-ran the full gate.

Screenshots, desktop and 390px phone width:

![devflow-start-worker-desktop](https://github.com/Adamniels/Personal-platform/blob/pr-screenshots/352/devflow-start-worker-desktop.png?raw=true)
![devflow-start-worker-phone](https://github.com/Adamniels/Personal-platform/blob/pr-screenshots/352/devflow-start-worker-phone.png?raw=true)
![devflow-worker-rebuild-desktop](https://github.com/Adamniels/Personal-platform/blob/pr-screenshots/352/devflow-worker-rebuild-desktop.png?raw=true)
![devflow-worker-rebuild-phone](https://github.com/Adamniels/Personal-platform/blob/pr-screenshots/352/devflow-worker-rebuild-phone.png?raw=true)

No before screenshots: this run resumed an interrupted one, and before screenshots are taken only in a new run, while the branch still equals `main`. The Workers panel before this change is `devflow-project-workers` from #349.

Not verified:
- A real worker built and started from the commands on a real project, against GitHub. The e2e tests check the commands' text, `StartCommandTests` checks their parts, and the image test checks the base image, but nothing here ran `docker build` on a real `.devflow/Dockerfile` fetched through the route. The owner checks this by making a key on a project's page and pasting both commands on the Mac mini.
- That 2 GB is enough memory for a real card. The experiment of 2026-11-16 peaked at 1.05 GiB on one task. `devflow/README.md` says to start at most two workers beside the hosted copy until it is measured.

## Doc changes

- `devflow/README.md`: new "Starting a worker", covering the three layers, the base image and its two users, the attribution setting, the format of `.devflow/`, the recipe route, the two commands, the memory rule (at most two workers beside the hosted copy on the Mac mini's 8 GB), and when a worker needs a rebuild. The settings, routes, table and page sections are updated to match.
- `devflow/docs/devflow-architecture.md`: "Workers" gains the three layers, why the recipe is handed out and `COPY` refused, and why the release builds the base image. The security section gains: the agent cannot read the worker's files, the key is never in the command, and a worker on an old recipe gets no work. Review round 1: the key passage now says the key reaches `curl` on stdin, why `-H "…$(…)"` would put it in `ps`, and that the test checks the process's arguments.
- `devflow/README.md`, review round 1: the start command reads the key's header on stdin, and the passage under it says why.
- `infra/hosted/README.md`: "What runs" and "The images" gain the base image that is built and never started, and `check.sh`'s two new cases. "The images" says every final stage runs as a user that is not root. The base image's entrypoint runs as root by design, and the passage now names it as the exception.
- `contracts/README.md`: `project.schema.json` and the recorded `commits-path.json`.
- `docs/README.md`: the index entries for `devflow/README.md` and the architecture document now name what they gained.
- Settled's command fetches the recipe from `<DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL>`, which does not resolve on the host, and passes the key to `curl` with `-H "…$(sed …)"`, which puts it in `ps`. The docs describe the command as built, see Decisions.

## Instructions ignored

None.

## Waits for the owner

This pull request carries `has-decision`, so the merge gate will not merge it. The owner reviews and merges it once the reviewer has approved it and the runner has given it `owner-decision`. One decision waits for him:

- Claude Code goes into the base image with `npm ci` from `devflow/worker/package-lock.json` (2.1.325, integrity pinned), symlinked onto PATH, rather than with `npm install -g` as Settled wrote. It follows the hosted images' lockfile rule.

Two ordinary decisions also depart from the start command as Settled wrote it, which Settled calls "the intent": the recipe is fetched from the public origin rather than `DEVFLOW_WORKER_URL`, and the key reaches `curl` on stdin rather than in `-H "…$(…)"`. Both are under Decisions the agent made.

Merging confirms it, and a comment changes it.

labels.name: owner-decision
labels.description: A decision the agent made waits for the owner's answer

labels.name: has-decision
labels.description: The implementer flagged a decision. Read by the gate and the runner, not a signal to the owner
